title: _cache keeps only live pack indexes and a unit cache that shrinks when pruned
goal: kbfacts.prune_indexes also removes the index files of other root sets unused for longer than a stated period, and the unit cache's slack prune reclaims the deleted rows' space (VACUUM or auto_vacuum), so a clone's _cache holds at most KEEP_INDEXES plus one index file per root set in use and a kbunits.sqlite near the size of the units it keeps, proven by a test within the ceiling that plants old index files of two root sets and a cache with more rows than its slack; today this clone's _cache holds 8 kbindex files (320 MB, one of another root set unused since 2026-10-05, which _same_root never prunes) and a 192 MB kbunits.sqlite for a kb whose fresh cache is about 65 MB; the docs state the rule and no measured size.

run: import os,sys,tempfile,time;sys.path.insert(0,"_tools");import kbfacts as k;d=tempfile.mkdtemp();old=time.time()-40*86400;names=["kbindex-rffffffff-"+"a"*16+".sqlite"]+["kbindex-"+k._root_key()+("%016x"%i)+".sqlite" for i in range(3)];[(open(os.path.join(d,n),"w").close(),os.utime(os.path.join(d,n),(old,old))) for n in names];k.prune_indexes(d,names[1]);left=sorted(os.listdir(d));print(left);sys.exit(0 if names[0] not in left and names[1] in left else 1)

gates.question: Does the pruning of other root sets' files also cover their unit caches (kbunits-r<hash>.sqlite, and kbunits.sqlite when the current root set has a key), by the same unused-for period as their index files?
options: Yes: prune_indexes removes them by mtime, and opening a unit cache marks it used
No: only index files; unit caches of other root sets stay
gates.recommendation: Yes: prune_indexes removes them by mtime, and opening a unit cache marks it used
gates.answer: Yes: prune_indexes removes them by mtime, and opening a unit cache marks it used

gates.question: How does the unit cache's slack prune reclaim the space of the rows it deletes: VACUUM after the prune, or auto_vacuum=INCREMENTAL?
options: VACUUM after a prune that deleted rows, outside the transaction
auto_vacuum=INCREMENTAL with PRAGMA incremental_vacuum stepped after the prune
gates.recommendation: VACUUM after a prune that deleted rows, outside the transaction
gates.answer: VACUUM after a prune that deleted rows, outside the transaction

notes: Premise (2026-10-09, benchmark review): the check collects no test (exit 2). ls -la _cache/*.sqlite on this clone: 7 kbindex-<fp>.sqlite of the public root set at 42 MB each (6 written within one minute by a test run), kbindex-r3a5da8a5-...sqlite of another root set unused since 2026-10-05 (37 MB), kbunits.sqlite 192 MB; kbfacts.prune_indexes keeps KEEP_INDEXES=4 beyond the current file of the current root set only (_same_root), and the unit cache's slack prune (UNIT_CACHE_SLACK=2) deletes rows without reclaiming the file. Ordered after ST-a5hhfp3z, which keys the unit cache per root set in the same functions. Free: no model runs. Premise run at plan (2026-10-09): the planted prune check fails (prune_indexes leaves the other root set's 40-day-old file). tests.py -k unit_cache collects ST-dvzdykit's test, which the work extends with the slack prune's space reclaim; it passes before the work and pins that a cached weighing equals a fresh one.
